author: high
claim: For every positive integer k and every positive integer solution (x,y) of x^2+y^2=k(xy+1) with x>=y and k>=2, the conjugate integer z=ky-x satisfies 0<=z<y; moreover z=0 implies k=y^2, while z>0 makes (y,z) a strictly smaller positive solution.
evidence: Let P(T)=T^2-kyT+(y^2-k). Since P(x)=0, the other root is z=ky-x, an integer, and xz=y^2-k. If z<0, then k-y^2=x(-z)>=x. But x=ky-z>=k+1, whereas k-y^2<=k-1, contradiction. Next P(y)=(2-k)y^2-k<0. Since x>=y and P(y) is nonzero, x>y. From P(y)=(y-x)(y-z)<0 and y-x<0, one gets y-z>0, hence z<y. If z=0 then xz=y^2-k gives k=y^2. If z>0, P(z)=0 yields z^2+y^2=k(yz+1), and max(y,z)=y<x=max(x,y).

glossary.k: the positive integer value of the quotient
glossary.x: the larger coordinate of a chosen positive solution
glossary.y: the smaller coordinate of a chosen positive solution
